rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report the authors' own UAV multispectral flights (Phantom 4, DJI multispectral camera, Table 1), NDVI and TCARI/OSAVI maps (Figures 3-4), a drying trial with WSN sensor data (Figure 5) and microbiological counts (Figure 6) on one farm in Grotte, Sicily.
rows.notes: The study uses UAV multispectral imagery (NDVI, TCARI/OSAVI) only to assess chlorophyll/vigour and decide harvest time for rosemary and sage. No thermal imaging, no water-stress assessment, no irrigation scheduling and no water-conservation outcome are reported; the mention of optimizing irrigation appears only in the introduction citing other work. The study at most supports the precondition (canopy chlorophyll/vigour mapping) of the claimed irrigation-scheduling support.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report own UAV flights, drying and microbiological data from the Grotte farm. Q2: Section 2.4 and 3.1 (Figure 3): UAV multispectral NDVI time series were used to individuate harvest time; rosemary was harvested when most plants had NDVI about 0.64 with flowering confirmed visually, sage when NDVI was about 0.59; Figure 4 shows TCARI/OSAVI and NDVI maps of the rows.
rows.notes: Own evidence is limited to the harvest-timing element of the passage: the authors applied NDVI thresholds to pick harvest dates for two crops at one site in a semi-arid Mediterranean farm. No thermal imaging, no precision irrigation or nutrient management workflow, no water-use efficiency, and no yield or quality outcome attributable to the monitoring are reported; 'effectiveness' is asserted rather than tested. Chlorophyll-TCARI/OSAVI relationships are taken from Haboudane et al. [63], not measured on the ground. Visual flowering checks were a confirmation, not an independent method establishing the result. Two crops at one farm; no limitations or dispersion statistics for the NDVI results.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report own UAV multispectral, drying-sensor and microbiological data from one farm in Grotte, Sicily.
rows.notes: The study does not measure water-use efficiency, irrigation or water stress; it has no thermal imaging and no precision irrigation workflow. Its own remote-sensing result concerns harvest timing via NDVI and chlorophyll-index mapping only, so there is no evidence on water conservation.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report own UAV, drying and microbiological data.
rows.notes: No CWSI, no irrigation scheduling, no water-savings measurement and no phenolic analysis appear anywhere in the study. The technology studied is UAV multispectral monitoring for harvest timing plus a photovoltaic-powered smart dryer, not CWSI-guided irrigation scheduling.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report own UAV, drying and microbiological data.
rows.notes: The study reports no irrigation treatment, no deficit regime, no CWSI and no phenolic or metabolite measurements; the only quality data are microbial counts before and after drying. It cannot support water savings or phenolic increases under CWSI-guided scheduling.

notes: Full text available (some paragraphs duplicated by PDF extraction but complete). Single-farm case study in Grotte, Sicily, on UAV multispectral vegetation indices for rosemary/sage harvest timing, a photovoltaic smart solar dryer with WSN monitoring, and microbiological quality before/after drying. Nothing in the study concerns irrigation, water stress, thermal imaging, CWSI or water-use efficiency; the review's attribution of irrigation-related claims to this study is not supported.
